title: Edge contract · hand-over (release bundle + manifest)
description: Edge contract, part 1 (Welle 10, owner 25.09.): what UNSaC hands to a consumer — one bundle per consumer (format unsac.bundle/1) and one manifest (unsac.manifest/1) with the sha256 of every file. A consumer reports back what it loaded with feedback-schema.json: loadedVersion (the release), loadedCommit (the manifest's `commit`) and loadedDigest (the manifest's sha256 of its bundle). Any edge that accepts this bundle and reports that feedback is as good for UNSaC as unsac-edge. Written from what i3x-v5 packages/uns-compiler/bundle.mjs emits. Transport: UNSaC delivers with POST <target endpoint>/v1/unsac/release, body = a delivery request (the manifest + the consumer's bundle), bearer = the target's secret; the edge answers with a receipt (HTTP 202 accepted / 409 refused). The receipt is NOT 'loaded': loaded comes later through the feedback contract.

ref.description: The branch or release name the bundle was compiled from (e.g. next). The commit is in the manifest, so the bundle's digest stays a digest of its CONTENT (same content = same digest, feedback-schema.json).

sources.description: The sources the bundle's signals come from, verbatim from their source files: what an edge needs to connect (endpoint, security, credentials by secret NAME only) and how often to read.

connection.description: As in the source file (e.g. OPC UA endpoint, securityMode, securityPolicy, auth).

commit.description: The full osf-schemas commit the release was compiled from; the consumer reports it back as loadedCommit (feedback-schema.json). It lives here and not in the bundles, so a bundle's digest does not change when only the commit does.

files.description: Published path → sha256 (hex) of its canonical JSON; the digest of bundles/<consumerId>.json is what the consumer reports as loadedDigest. Canonical form (the bytes that are hashed): UTF-8 JSON, object keys sorted by UTF-16 code unit, 2-space indentation, one element per line, LF line ends, exactly one trailing LF, empty array [] and empty object {}, -0 written as 0, no undefined/NaN/Infinity. A consumer recomputes sha256 over exactly these bytes.

signalId.description: <instance>/<property> — the name UNSaC and every consumer use for this signal.

instance.description: Instance id of the plant tree (e.g. the machine).

path.description: ISA-95 equipment path of the instance, or null.

sourceNode.description: Address of the value in the source (OPC UA NodeId, MTConnect DataItem, column …).

deliveryRequest.description: What UNSaC POSTs to <endpoint>/v1/unsac/release. The edge checks sha256(canonical bundle) against manifest.files['bundles/<consumerId>.json'] before it accepts.

digest.description: sha256 of the bundle as the edge received it.

reason.description: Why a delivery was refused (accepted false).
